title: XSS
body:
Cross-Site Scripting is an attack where an attacker gets their own JavaScript to execute inside your page, in your users' browsers. The classic vector is unescaped user input rendered straight into the page — a review body containing a `<script>` tag, for instance — which is why setting `innerHTML` from untrusted data is dangerous and `textContent` is not.

Once attacker JS runs on your origin, it has everything your own code has: it can read [[localStorage]], call your [[API]] with the user's session, and rewrite the [[DOM]]. This is the concrete reason `HttpOnly` exists on cookies — an HttpOnly session cookie is invisible to injected JS, whereas a JWT sitting in localStorage can simply be read and exfiltrated. Defences are output escaping, a Content Security Policy, and never trusting input from the [[Client]]. Contrast with [[CSRF]].
